findings.title: check_cancels decodes Minswap's swap with no nesting check of its own; it is safe today only because inspect runs check_nesting first
findings.scenario: Minswap's build-tx returns a swap whose witness set carries a datum (or an output whose inline datum is) nested a few thousand levels deep. The 1.6.0 review found that depth overflows WebAssembly's stack when Pallas decodes it, which traps the module (pool.rs:271-278). checkOrderCancels (check_cancels) decodes the whole swap at orders.rs:1232 with no depth walk of its own. Today nothing reaches it: its only caller, sessions.ts cancelsChecked (sessions.ts:4425), runs after inspectSessionTx (sessions.ts:4393). That goes through cip30::inspect, which calls check_nesting(&bytes) before decoding (cip30.rs:1139, 1149) and refuses the swap first. Moving the dry run ahead of the inspect, for example to save a WebAssembly call, or adding a second caller of the public binding, would let a bad build trap the module during a swap's review.
findings.evidence: orders.rs:1231-1232: `pub fn check_cancels(s: &SwapCheck) -> Result<Vec<CancelCheck>> { let tx = MultiEraTx::decode(s.tx_cbor)...`. order_at (orders.rs:1303-1320) then reads `data.raw_cbor()` and `tx.plutus_data()`, so Pallas has decoded every datum by then. uplc and Pallas decode PlutusData recursively (cbor.rs:3-7 says so; pool.rs:274-278 records the 1.6.0 overflow, 314-wasm#0). Core has no whole-transaction guard. `rg within_depth|MAX_DEPTH` over seedelf-core/src and wasm/src finds only per-datum and per-output checks (pool.rs:152,280; mod.rs:381; orders.rs:444; eval.rs:82). The wasm crate's check_nesting (cip30.rs:680), which also walks tag-24-wrapped bytes (cip30.rs:575-625), runs in inspect (cip30.rs:1149) and decode.rs:624. It does not run in check_order_cancels (lib.rs:888-905), which calls check_cancels directly. Caller order: sessions.ts:4393 `wasm.inspectSessionTx(...)`, then sessions.ts:4425 `await this.cancelsChecked(...)`, the only call site (`rg checkOrderCancels` finds sessions.ts:4280 alone). git blame orders.rs:1231-1234 gives 5f7a405af.
findings.fix: Hold any whole transaction core decodes from outside the wallet to the depth limit in core itself. Move cip30's nests_within/check_nesting, which walks wrapped byte strings too, into seedelf-core's cbor module and call it at the top of check_cancels, refusing with the same words. The wasm crate then calls the moved function. Others of this class in core: none in this lane. launched_pool (eval::resolve_outputs) and with_integrity decode only the wallet's own transactions.
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md and archive/plans/*.md for check_cancels, checkOrderCancels, check_order_cancels, order_at, and nest/depth near order, cancel, swap or minswap: none. The 1.6.0 review's 314-wasm#0 covered a pool's script rows, not the swap.

guards.stops: Trusting a pool whose NFT policy isn't one_shot_mint(seed) (WrongSeed), or whose datum names M/L/F other than the templates applied to that seed (WrongScripts). Every address and reward account comes from the derived scripts.

A reference candidate that isn't at the holder on this network, has a stake credential or a reference script, holds anything but one lovejoin NFT and ADA, or is a 10 ₳ ADA copy (candidate, lines 331-351)
A reference datum outside one_shot_mint's ranges (box_lovelace>0, 0<max_fee<box_lovelace, token fields sane, 28-byte hashes, exactly 8 fields)
An output at the holder nested past 128 levels being decoded (WebAssembly stack overflow), as a reference or a script row
Reading mix_box or mix_logic by reference from a UTxO that isn't at the never-spent holder, or isn't byte-for-byte the derived PlutusV3 script; otherwise the script is carried
New boxes in a pool whose box is under today's min-UTxO (BelowMinimum); CantComeBack when a box can't pay its own way back (lines 637-641)
Launching a pool of a Seedelf identifier token, or a 10 ₳ ADA pool (check_terms)
A launch whose datum one_shot_mint would refuse, which would fail its mint (round trip through ReferenceDatum::decode)
A launch whose own outputs don't make a pool the wallet trusts and reads by reference (verify_derived, inline_scripts empty)
A launch whose boxes couldn't be made or come back (check_usable, called at 182 and 406)
guards.test: seedelf-core/tests/lovejoin_launch_test.rs:202 (a box too small to come back)

guards.stops: A private launch spending a Seedelf UTxO that holds tokens (they would go with the change)
An account launch whose inputs can't cover the three outputs, the deposit and the fee (checked subtraction, ACCOUNT_LAUNCH_SHORT)
An account launch whose collateral return would be under its minimum after 3/2 of the fee (fee even, so exact)
An account launch spending a UTxO the evaluator refuses (a stranger's reference script), which would have the launch refused
Signing a launch whose finished bytes don't make a verified pool reading its scripts from the holder (launched_pool)
Treating as the session's an order another key cancels, or one that pays anyone but base(session payment, session stake) (Session::owns)
Accepting an order no cancel can spend: an inline datum at a Plutus V1 script, or a script on it (unspendable)
Decoding an order datum nested past 128 levels (WebAssembly stack overflow)
A SundaeSwap V4 order with a chained datum, or constraint modules other than basic_order then fee_constraint, which could leave a remnant
A Splash datum whose twelve fields aren't of the types its script decodes (an order the script could never spend)
A bundled Plutus V1 order script that isn't the pinned hash; a row with no place, or two, to read its script from
A cancel's collateral holding tokens or a datum
A cancel built on a datum other than the one the order holds inline or names by hash
Reading an order's script from a reference that doesn't hold the pinned script
A cancel spending a session row that holds a datum or a script (a stranger's)
Overflow in the decision to leave an exact 5 ₳ collateral behind, on an order reported near u64::MAX
A Splash cancel whose output 0 isn't the order's exact value at the session's address
A collateral return under an output's least, or a collateral that can't cover 3/2 of the fee
Sending a cancel whose declared budgets don't cover what its scripts measured
A cancel carrying a witness datum (a Plutus V1 order's) being refused at submit for Pallas's wrong script data hash; also the V1 legacy language view

checked_ok: verify_pool holds against a pool launcher. A trusted pool's scripts are always templates(seed, set). P must equal the NFT's policy, and the datum's M, L and F must equal the derived ones. Protocol takes mix_box_hash, mix_logic_hash, fee_hash and id from the derived scripts, never from the datum (pool.rs:403-485).

derive_for: the datum's L picks the set. An unknown L falls back to V2's scripts and is refused as WrongScripts. A V1-set pool launched today still verifies, as TokenV1, and is retired in the worker (lovejoin.ts:691 isRetired: version !== 'v2'), so it takes no new boxes.

ReferenceDatum::decode accepts no datum one_shot_mint would refuse; Lovejoin 29573c5's datum_sane and token_sane were read side by side. It is stricter only in form: tag 121 only, small-int encoding, exactly 8 fields, 28-byte hashes. That can hide a pool but never trusts a wrong one.

Only one P.lovejoin can ever exist. one_shot_mint takes exactly one asset name, quantity 1, and the seed consumed. reference_holder errors in every context (proved: Lovejoin.AnyTx.PurposesKernel.reference_holder_every_context_errors), so the datum mix_logic reads (read_reference_datum: exactly one carrier) can't change or be duplicated.
REFERENCE_HOLDER template hashes to 288fea77… (recomputed: blake2b_224(0x03‖bytes)), matching REFERENCE_HOLDER_HASH.
mix_logic and mix_box read the datum's mix_script_hash. The wallet requires it to equal mix_box(L), so boxes sit where the scripts look.

pool_of reads a script by reference only from a PlutusV3 script ref at this network's holder, which is never spendable, with bytes equal to the derived script. Otherwise it carries the script. Never both, so no extraneous witness.

Launch: the datum round-trips through decode before anything is built. Each output holds exactly its min-UTxO (least_at_holder settles in 2 steps at these sizes, all 4-byte coin encodings). The pool is verified from the made outputs (verify_derived) and again from the finished bytes (launched_pool) before the wasm crate signs (lib.rs:2611, 2702).

Account launch balances: inputs = the 3 outputs + change + deposit + fee, with tokens to change and the minted NFT to output 0. The collateral return is collateral − 3/2·fee with its tokens, the fee is even, and the return is held to its minimum.
Locked figures equal the tx's outputs. The deposit really never comes back: mix_logic's publish allows only RegisterCredential, so the credential can't be deregistered.

launch_apart: every seed's pool locks and costs the same (hash-sized params), and is made once per seed. The private launch's rows pass check_spendable (owned, no Seedelf, no evaluator refusal, lib.rs:2316-2342). launch_from_account filters eval::refusal rows.
A private launch in launch_apart always spends its seed: it is the first of the inputs ScriptSpend::new spends. The account launch's every prefix starts with spendable[0].

orders.json: each bundled Plutus V1 script (minswap-v1, sundae-v1, wingriders-v1) hashes to its pinned hash (recomputed with the 0x01 tag). Every pinned referenceSize equals the fixture script's byte length (2659, 1128, 2469, 2380, 417, 1072, 3128). No duplicate script per network.

Cancel redeemers match the real cancels in fixtures/order_cancels.json: Constr 1 [] for Minswap V1/V2/Stable, Sundae V1/V3/Stable and WingRiders V1/V2; Constr 0 [] for Splash (False) and Sundae V4 (Cancel).

integrity_hash: the V1 legacy view (key bytes(0x00), value bytes(indefinite int list)) and the V2/V3 views (uint key, definite list) match the ledger. Witness datums are hashed as the tx carries them: Pallas's NonEmptySet always writes tag 258 (pallas-codec 0.35 utils.rs:858-870), while pallas-txbuilder hashes a plain Vec (scriptdata.rs ScriptData::hash). with_integrity re-encodes the same structures it hashes, so the hashed bytes are the sent bytes.

A hash-kept datum that Pallas would re-encode differently (non-minimal ints, odd chunking) can't reach a signed swap. uplc looks witness datums up by their bytes' hash (script_context.rs:141, 841), so the dry run fails MissingRequiredDatum and the swap is refused as not cancellable.
ledger_positions sorts inputs by (tx id, index) exactly as pallas-txbuilder does (conway.rs:46), so budgets are matched by spend index.

Every cancel output goes to the session's address, with Splash's exact refund at output 0. The fee comes off lovelace_in by checked subtraction. The worker refuses a cancel paying anyone else, or with a fee over 3 ₳ (sessions.ts:4196-4197).

check_cancels: stand-in outpoints (hash of swap id ‖ tag) can't collide with the order. Each order is dry-run alone. Stop's grouping by Plutus version is tested with each protocol's real script (orders_test.rs:936). Measured cancel budgets are 0.02-0.31M mem, so a group can't approach MAX_TX_BUDGET.

Session::owns needs the canceller to be the session's key (the stake key for Sundae V3, V4 and Stable) and every payee to be base(payment, stake). The table's V1 entries are inline-only, so a V1 cancel has no reference input, as the ledger and uplc (ScriptAndInputRefNotAllowed) require.

The worker's plainAda and collateralFits (sessions.ts:1052, 1081) exclude rows with a reference script or datum. cancel_orders' unchecked collateral reference script (it would fail at resolve_row) is unreachable.
The private launch's cert 0 race: a front-runner registering L first only gets the launch refused in phase 1, at 2 ₳ locked of their own each time. No collateral is taken.
notes: For the owner, a new fact on the settled trust in Minswap (architecture.md:651: 'an aggregator acting in bad faith could take up to the funded swap amount either way'). orders::read for MinswapV2 (orders.rs:462-469) reads fields 0, 1 and 3 and ignores field 8, expiry_setting_opt: Option<(expired_time, max_tip)>. The repo's own reading of minswap-dex-v2 says that with an expiry set, anyone may cancel the order after it for a tip of at most max_tip, the rest going to the refund receiver (flows.md:457; chunk-15-dapp-connector.md:150: the SDK's default tip is 0.3 ₳). So a V2 order with Some((t, tip)) passes Session::owns and the owner-cancel dry run, yet after t it pays up to `tip` lovelace to whoever cancels it, not only the session. Both real V2 orders in fixtures/order_cancels.json carry None (decoded: 9 fields, last Constr 1 []), so nothing reaches this today. A bad-faith build is within the stated trust. architecture.md:650's 'The reader vouches for who cancels an order and whom it pays' is a little wider than the reader for V2 (for D1). If ever wanted: read field 8 and refuse Some, or hold max_tip to a small cap (a new refusal: the owner's).

The same class as backlog ❓ L9 (V4's max_per_execution): the reader holds no order's fee fields to the quote: Minswap V1/Stable batcher fee and deposit (fields 4, 5), V2 max_batcher_fee (7), Sundae V1 scooper fee (2), V3/Stable max_protocol_fee (2), WingRiders V2's oil (0), Splash's cost per step and fee. Only withinFunding bounds them, as architecture.md says for V4. I couldn't check offline whether WingRiders V1/V2 let anyone reclaim after their deadline field, nor for whom; their payees (beneficiary, and owner for V2) are both held to the session, so funds would still come back.

verify_pool runs derive_for (4-5 template applications) before comparing P, though policy_of (one application) would refuse a wrong seed first. It's harmless: the seed comes from the bundled list, the data layer, or find_seed, which already matched P. The doc's 'cheapest first' holds only for the shape checks.

The pool reader hides, never wrongly trusts, some pools one_shot_mint would mint: a reference datum with constructor 0 in tag-102 form, a small int in big-int form, or other tokens beside the NFT at the reference output (output_at_reference_holder checks only quantity_of(NFT) == 1). No money is at stake. It also matches what the data layer's copy should do; worth confirming in its vectors if that lane looks.

cancel_orders spends every plain-ADA row the worker passes (sessions.ts cancelOf: `funds: plain`). A stranger's dust (hundreds of ADA-only UTxOs) could push the cancel past 16 KiB (TooLarge) and pause Stop. It costs them about 1 ₳ a row, roughly 400 ₳ to reach the limit, all of which the session keeps, so it isn't credible. Picking the fewest rows that pay would end it anyway.

AccountLaunch's collateral may be any UTxO from `available`, including one the evaluable filter left out for a reference script. That's fine as far as I can tell: the ledger counts reference scripts only on spending and reference inputs, and the evaluator never sees the collateral. Worth one live check if a stranger ever sends the account such a UTxO.
templates.rs is frozen and I report no consequence. Every application is tested against real pools (preprod and mainnet's v2 5 ₳ pool), and reference_holder's always-false is kernel-proved.
coverage: Read in full: seedelf-core/src/lovejoin/pool.rs (645 lines), launch.rs (796), orders.rs (1518), and templates.rs' code (lines 1-230); its hex constants were skimmed, frozen. orders.json was decoded entry by entry; the V1 scripts' hashes and every referenceSize were recomputed. Followed out of the lane: lovejoin/mod.rs 1-640 (Protocol, Version, mix_box_address, deposit_reference, reference_script_size, PoolBox, Rewards). In the wasm crate: lovejoin.rs protocol_of and PoolView (150-320, 660-700); lib.rs' launch builders (2470-2780), order bindings (640-940), check_spendable (2300-2345) and inspect_session_tx; cip30.rs check_nesting and inspect (575-690, 1139-1150). In the extension: sessions.ts cancel, cancelOf, cancelsChecked, referenceRows and inspect (4150-4440), plainAda and collateralFits, and lovejoin.ts isRetired. Lovejoin 29573c5's one_shot_mint.ak, reference_holder.ak, reference.ak, types.ak, mix_logic.ak, mix_box.ak and mixbox.ak. pallas-txbuilder 0.35 conway.rs and scriptdata.rs, pallas-codec NonEmptySet, pallas-primitives' Conway Tx and WitnessSet, and uplc 1.1.23's datum lookup. I decoded the real order datums in tests/fixtures/order_cancels.json (MinswapV2 x2, WingRiders V1/V2/StableV2, Minswap V1, MinswapStable, Sundae V1). Tests were skimmed for pins: orders_test.rs (test list and several bodies), lovejoin_pools_test.rs (verify_pool negatives), lovejoin_launch_test.rs (refusals). Not reached: build.rs's ScriptSpend internals (settle, select_script_inputs, mint_inline, with_staking balance), lovejoin/mod.rs past 640 (withdraw and mix; R3a's), box_value.rs and value.rs, and the worker's pool discovery and launch flows (lovejoin-pools.ts, lovejoin-launch.ts). Minswap V2's and WingRiders' on-chain sources weren't available offline: the V2 expiry-tip semantics come from the repo's own reading of them (flows.md:457, chunk-15). No tests were run.
